endorsements.quote: By requiring very large online platforms to publish transparency reports on content moderation, conduct independent audits of recommendation algorithms, and establish accessible appeals mechanisms, the DSA attempts to make the platform’s quasi-regulatory function formally accountable.

unlisted_practices: Regulators should adopt adaptive, risk-calibrated regulatory architectures, such as regulatory sandboxes and proportionate regulation, in place of one-size-fits-all compliance frameworks.

Platforms should build transparent, auditable moderation frameworks covering rule publication, determination, review, appeal, and feedback, with human-comprehensible explanations for moderation decisions.

Regulators should design tiered compliance-cost architectures that apply the highest-intensity requirements to high-risk procedures by large actors and proportionate burdens to smaller operators in lower-risk activities.

Industry associations should provide shared compliance infrastructure, such as contract templates, training resources, self-assessment tools, and shared adverse-event reporting systems, to reduce compliance costs for smaller operators.

Regulators should institutionalize circuit-breaker mechanisms that trigger staged impact assessments before further regulatory tightening when market indicators such as operator exit rate, compliance-cost index, or concentration ratio breach thresholds.
Regulators should use incentive-compatible governance designs that reward compliant behavior, such as preferential algorithmic treatment and reduced deposit requirements.
Platforms should contribute their data assets to a shared safety-monitoring infrastructure to support population-level adverse-event surveillance.
Industry associations should develop cross-platform governance harmonization reference frameworks to reduce divergent rule environments.

screen.reason: This is a theoretical framework and policy/governance paper proposing a triadic co-evolutionary framework (ITP model) for public health and platform governance in digital service sectors (specifically medical esthetics commerce in China with generative AI). It contains no primary empirical evaluation of an AI tool.
